A.why: Honest A-line gown with crimson waist and bone hem, but almost entirely black: from the ARPG camera it merges into one dark slab.
A.fix: Add a lighter slate/stone wimple-capelet or an amber/crimson front stole so the gown reads at night from above.

B.why: Clearest gown silhouette: fitted violet sash and a stepped A-line skirt to the floor, plus a choir stole on the bodice; holds on the slim avatar.
B.fix: Replace the off-palette cyan collar with amber/bone, and soften the staircase skirt tiers.

C.why: A straight column of horizontal bands plus gold studs reads as lamellar/studded armour; the cyan bands are off-palette.
C.fix: Taper at the waist and flare the skirt; remove the studs and cyan.

D.why: Best theme: a spire headpiece like the church tower, and real stained-glass panes. But the skirt is a straight segmented tube, with no waist or flare.
D.fix: Give it a crimson waist and a two-tier flare; gather the scattered panes into one lancet panel.

E.why: Biggest, most distinct skirt from above, with a nice wet-stone waterline idea, but the bottom tier is a hollow, gappy frame. It is squat, wide-shouldered, and the cap looks like a mortarboard.
E.fix: Close the hollow hem ring into a solid sloped tier, and narrow and lengthen the skirt.

F.why: Most elegant palette (bone cuffs, violet panel, crimson jewel, slate hem), and the violet stripe reads at night. But the straight skirt reads as a cassock.
F.fix: Flare the skirt from hip to shins and add a short low veil behind the cap.

notes: No candidate fully lands. B has the gown silhouette, F the palette and elegance, D the theme (spire plus stained glass), and E's flood-line hem is a good idea. A merge would win: B's skirt shape, F's colours and violet panel, D's stained-glass panel as a bodice window, and E's slate waterline hem. Across the batch: sleeves are broad default blocks, thin pinstripe trims are invisible from above, and cyan appears in B and C although it is off-brief.
